title: UNC5B regulates epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition through a SRC-ZEB1 signaling axis to facilitate pancreatic cancer metastasis
task: Identify and validate UNC5B as a central regulator of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and metastasis in pancreatic cancer
key_results: UNC5B loss completely abolished metastatic spread, reduced tumor proliferation, increased intratumoral necrosis, and preserved epithelial morphology in KPCU and orthotopic models; UNC5B drives EMT specifically through SRC-ZEB1 axis without affecting SNAIL or TWIST1; targeted degradation reduced EMT scores and ZEB1/SRC levels
comments: Elegant genetic and pharmacological validation identifies UNC5B as a central metastasis hub; specificity for ZEB1 over other EMT factors suggests therapeutic selectivity.

model_io.model: genetically engineered KPCU mouse model with Unc5b loss
orthotopic pancreatic cancer xenografts with Unc5b loss
PDAC cells with UNC5B protein degrader (degron)

hypotheses.hypothesis: UNC5B loss abolishes metastatic dissemination in vivo
hypotheses.result: confirmed in both KPCU and orthotopic models; no invasion or lymph node involvement

hypotheses.hypothesis: UNC5B drives EMT specifically through SRC-ZEB1 axis
hypotheses.result: confirmed; ZEB1 engagement without alteration of SNAIL or TWIST1

hypotheses.hypothesis: Pharmacological UNC5B degradation recapitulates genetic loss phenotype
hypotheses.result: confirmed; marked reduction in EMT scores and decreased ZEB1/SRC

title: The anti-tumour activity of TNF in melanoma is determined by cFLIP
task: Determine whether cFLIP expression determines melanoma susceptibility to TNF-induced cell death and controls tumor growth
key_results: cFlipKO/KO B16F10 melanoma cells failed to grow in wild-type mice but formed tumors in TNF-deficient mice; TNF alone sufficient to control cFlipKO/KO melanoma; cIAP or RIPK1 ablation did not trigger TNF cytotoxicity or affect melanoma growth in vivo, in contrast to cFLIP
comments: Challenges conventional model of TNF-induced apoptosis via cIAP/RIPK1; identifies cFLIP as specific checkpoint independent of canonical RIPK1-dependent pathways, suggesting novel therapeutic opportunity.

model_io.model: syngeneic B16F10 melanoma model in wild-type and TNF-deficient mice
B16F10 melanomas with cIAP or RIPK1 genomic ablation

hypotheses.hypothesis: cFLIP expression protects melanoma cells from TNF-induced cell death
hypotheses.result: confirmed; cFlipKO/KO cells sensitive to TNF in vivo (wild-type mice), resistant in TNF-deficient mice

hypotheses.hypothesis: cIAP and RIPK1 are not essential for TNF-induced control of melanoma lacking cFLIP
hypotheses.result: confirmed; cIAP or RIPK1 ablation alone did not affect melanoma growth

hypotheses.hypothesis: cFLIP targeting could enhance TNF-based immunotherapy efficacy
hypotheses.result: supported by data showing cFLIP-dependent TNF sensitivity determines melanoma growth

title: Epigenetics drives oocyte aging: from mechanisms to interventions
task: Review mechanisms of epigenetic aging in oocytes and therapeutic interventions
key_results: DNA methylation, histone modifications, RNA modifications, and ncRNA dysregulation impair meiosis and developmental competence; NAD+ precursors and sirtuin activation show mechanistic promise
comments: Comprehensive review highlighting the gap between mechanistic understanding and translational applicability of epigenetic interventions in aged oocytes.

title: Aging of the neural stem cell niche: integration of local and muscle-derived systemic signals in preclinical and translational contexts
task: Characterize how systemic muscle-derived signals integrate with local niche cells to regulate neural stem cell aging
key_results: Skeletal muscle sends myokines, metabolites, and vascular signals that influence NSC niche function; exercise and muscle health preservation protect brain regenerative capacity
comments: Highlights emerging evidence that systemic aging signals from periphery may rival local brain aging factors in controlling NSC function.

title: Integrated computational and in vitro analysis reveals the toxic mechanisms of PFAS in female diminished ovarian reserve
task: Elucidate mechanisms by which PFAS exposure contributes to diminished ovarian reserve through integrated computational and experimental analysis
key_results: 35 candidate PFAS targets identified; core targets regulate cell proliferation, immune-inflammatory, and hormone signaling pathways; PFAS induces dose- and time-dependent KGN cell cytotoxicity and oxidative stress via BAX upregulation, Bcl-2 downregulation, GSTP1/PRDX5 suppression, AMH/INHB inhibition, and TGFBR1-mediated pro-fibrotic signaling
comments: Comprehensive multi-omics approach links environmental exposure to female infertility through apoptosis, oxidative stress, and fibrosis mechanisms; clinical validation in DOR patients remains needed.

model_io.model: network toxicology, machine learning, molecular docking, MD simulation
KGN cells exposed to PFAS

hypotheses.hypothesis: PFAS perturbs pathways governing cell proliferation, immune-inflammatory responses, and hormone signaling
hypotheses.result: confirmed by GO and KEGG enrichment analyses

hypotheses.hypothesis: PFAS induces KGN cell apoptosis and oxidative stress
hypotheses.result: confirmed; dose- and time-dependent cytotoxicity with BAX upregulation and Bcl-2 downregulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: PFAS impairs ovarian reserve by suppressing AMH and INHB synthesis
hypotheses.result: confirmed in KGN cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: PFAS activates pro-fibrotic signaling via TGFBR1 upregulation
hypotheses.result: confirmed

title: Octa-arginine-modified calcium phosphate nanoparticles with amiloride enhance gene delivery and bone augmentation in rat calvaria
task: Optimize R8-modified calcium phosphate nanoparticles with amiloride for enhanced gene delivery and bone regeneration
key_results: Amiloride increased transfection efficiency by modulating intracellular pH and Ca2+ dynamics; R8-CaP+amiloride+BMP-2 plasmid achieved highest local BMP-2 concentration and significantly enhanced bone formation in rat calvaria, though less than exogenous 2 µg BMP-2 protein
comments: Achieves significant synergistic effect but fails to match protein benchmark; mechanism of amiloride cytotoxicity partially mitigated by R8 warrants further optimization.
